Project Overview

The Nuclear Decommissioning Authority (NDA) PhD Studentship at Lancaster University focuses on understanding the longitudinal challenges of applying guardrails to Artificial Intelligence in the nuclear sector. This is a 42-month funded project, including fees and an enhanced stipend.

Project Details

The nuclear sector is exploring the use of AI to support various functions, including operational technology (OT). Guardrails are socio-technical measures to protect systems from errant AI behaviour. This PhD will investigate a framework that supports risk-informed decisions about the choice of guardrails for ensuring safe and secure operation of nuclear functions, focusing on case studies that incorporate AI for improving security and efficiency of OT. The framework should consider characteristics of guardrails (cost, flexibility, scrutability, effectiveness) and how they are affected by longitudinal drift.

Supervisor

Professor Paul Smith, School of Computing and Communications, Lancaster University.

Entry Requirements

  • Applicants must have a Master’s degree and/or a minimum of a 2:1 in their bachelor’s degree in computer science or a related field.
  • Applicants must be resident in the UK during the period of study; they may need to travel to collect data during their studies and will need to obtain security clearance.
  • Expected primary fieldwork site will be in Cumbria.

Funding

  • 42-month funded project, including fees and an enhanced stipend.

How to Apply

Applications should be submitted via the standard admissions process. You must provide an up-to-date CV, two references, a written statement of purpose, and a further piece of research/assignment work, dissertation section, or publication is recommended.

Contact

Applicants can contact Professor Paul Smith to discuss their applications.
